reels.caption:
If you can run 3 miles, you’re ready to tackle marathon training. 

On this episode of The Amazing Runner’s World Show, Jeff and Matt talk about the key components of race training.

Watch the full episode at the link in our bio.🔗

How I structure my marathon training 👇🏼

My weeks consist of:
- Easy runs (~70% of total volume)
- Long runs (either easy or tempo blocks)
- Tempo runs (track sessions, mid long run tempo blocks)
- Strength training (2x Upper body, 1x Legs and core)
- Cross training (swimming and cycling) 

I also try to integrate one rest day. I either take the full day off or do a super light session - can be a run, swim, or bike ride.

Hope that helps👌🏼

John Heymans’s recent coaching advice emphasizes that marathon training is more than just mileage—it requires building aerobic fitness, fueling, recovery, and cross training before starting a formal plan ¹. Most beginners need 18 to 20 weeks to prepare, starting with a base of three to four easy runs weekly and gradually increasing distance by no more than 10 percent per week to avoid injury ² ³.

posts.caption: How to train for your first marathon #marathon #marathontraining #runner #running #runstagram

🏃‍♀️ How I’d train for a marathon from ZERO (with just 4 runs/week)

When people think “marathon training” they picture 60-mile weeks, sore knees, and zero free time. But the truth? You can build up to 26.2 without your life falling apart—if you follow a simple structure.

Here’s how I’d set it up ⬇️

✨ 2 easy runs → slow, comfortable pace, just getting time on your feet.
✨ 1 long run → start with 3–4 miles, add about 1 mile each week.
✨ 1 speed/strength run → intervals, hills, or strides to build endurance and leg power.

That’s it. No magic, no overcomplication. Consistency beats going “all …[truncated]

training for your first marathon doesn’t have to be daunting 😉 if you follow a few basic tips you’ll get through it just fine and no matter what, you’ll be so proud of yourself (and inspire so many people around you!).
these 5 tips are at the top of the list imo👇🏼

1. GRADUAL is the word of the cycle! I like to prescribe runs every other day with 1 being a long run—where you’ll increase by 1/2mi to 1mi every week. Once you get through a few weeks, then start adding a little to your other runs. Speed work isn’t absolutely necessary as a beginner, but if you’re following a program that has some,…[truncated]

🚨 Save and share these training tips 👆

Ideally, every aspiring marathoner should have been a recreational runner for at least a year before embarking on a marathon training program.

If you start from cero to building weekly mileage too soon, you’ll get injured very fast.  So follow these basic “rules” for marathon training:

⚡️ BUILD A BASE MILEAGE 
Run consistently at least 20–30 miles a week and start small by signing up to shorter races like 5Ks, 10Ks, etc. 
 
⚡️ SPEED WORK
Practice intervals and tempo runs to increase your cardio capacity.

⚡️LONG RUNS
Do a distance run once a week so yo…[truncated]

My week of workouts Marathon Training! Training Structure below ⬇️

🏃🏽‍♀️ I make sure to always have an easy day in between my “harder effort” days.

👉🏼 this week looked like this:
• Monday - medium long run
• Tuesday - easy run
• Wednesday - speed workout
• Thursday - easy cross train (pavement break)
• Friday - Long Run
• Saturday - recovery hike 🙃

This split helps me get my mileage in while preventing injuries during a marathon training cycle.

16 MILES!!!! 🥹 My furthest run EVER.

I’m just so proud of myself. The last few miles started to get really tough, and I literally had to start talking to myself out loud — “I can do this. I’m strong. Keep going.”

And I did 🥹

So grateful I got to run this one with my dad because having him there helped me more than he probably knows. 16 miles down and feeling very proud of how far I’ve come in this marathon training 🤍

items.desc: marathon training is teaching me a lot more than how to run 26.2 miles 🥹 learning to trust myself, give myself grace, pivot when I need to, and stop caring about what my training looks like compared to everyone else. the goal isn’t perfect training. it’s making it to the start line healthy, happy & proud of how I got there 🤍 #marathontraining #runtok #runningcommunity #runningmotivation #runnergirl

Day 28 of marathon training 😭 I know these videos might feel a little repetitive because lately I’ve only been getting a few miles in, but I’m genuinely trying my best out here. 🥲 Between school, work, and trying to train for a whole MARATHON, I’m learning that sometimes getting a few miles in is still better than doing nothing at all. It might not look like a lot right now, but I’m still showing up. And honestly, that’s what matters. One mile at a time. #Day28 #MarathonTraining #MarathonJourney #RunnerTok #RunTok @Oner Active @Every Woman’s Marathon
